briefing.headline: OpenAI Orion-2 and xAI Colossus-3 push frontier capabilities as US tightens export controls on advanced chips

sections.label: EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
sections.text: Frontier labs released multiple high-capability models this month while regulatory pressure on compute exports intensified. Funding remains robust at $11.9B for the quarter with major infrastructure deals accelerating.

sections.label: FRONTIER MODELS
sections.text: OpenAI deployed Orion-2 internally with reported gains on long-horizon reasoning. xAI launched Colossus-3 on 1.2M H200 cluster. DeepSeek-R2 matched GPT-5 level on select benchmarks at lower inference cost.

sections.label: SAFETY & SECURITY
sections.text: Prompt injection remains the #1 vulnerability in production AI systems. DialectForge's dynamic dialect negotiation is designed to solve injection at the protocol level for multi-agent, automotive, and BCI deployments.

sections.label: COMPUTE & INFRASTRUCTURE
sections.text: Microsoft announced two new 200MW data centers in Texas dedicated to OpenAI training. TSMC began volume production of 2nm process for AI accelerators with first shipments to Google and Amazon.

sections.label: STRATEGIC QUESTION
sections.text: Will export controls on advanced chips slow Chinese frontier progress more than they accelerate domestic alternatives?
